comments.author: @tysoncung
comments.text: The part that stuck with me: some stretches of the Namib coast get as little as two millimetres of rain a year, yet can sit under thick fog for more than 180 days, blown in off the cold Benguela current. The water arrives sideways instead of falling. Sources are linked in the description if you want to dig into the numbers. Where you live, is there a weather feature everyone treats as scenery that is actually doing real work?
